anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, likely used to format this dataset; it does not describe the Muse sleep-onset EEG data.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard extension for EEG that this dataset's BIDS format follows; it does not describe the Muse sleep-onset data.

metadata.methods_description: Recordings were made at home by participants using a Muse S family headband with four dry EEG channels (TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10), stored at 128 Hz (downsampling from 256 Hz is a curator-supplied assumption). Each recording lasts about 6 to 30 minutes and ends 300 s after the annotated first N2 epoch. Data were exported to BrainVision format with pybv and organized according to EEG-BIDS.
